items.title: Compact phase-generator mixture
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, with its Borel sigma-algebra, and let $a:K\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. The **convex hull** $\operatorname{conv}K$ is the set of finite convex combinations of points of $K$. A **phase generator** is a point $y\in K$ with declared energy $a(y)$. A **mixture** is a Borel probability measure $P$ on $K$. Its barycenter and mean energy are the coordinatewise Lebesgue integrals
$$\bar y(P):=\int_K y\,dP(y)\in\mathbb R^d,\qquad \bar a(P):=\int_K a(y)\,dP(y)\in\mathbb R.$$
These integrals are finite because each coordinate and $a$ are bounded on compact $K$. For prescribed mean $x\in\operatorname{conv}K$, the **mixture energy** is
$$a_{\rm mix}(x):=\inf\{\bar a(P):P\text{ is a Borel probability on }K,\ \bar y(P)=x\}.$$
The admissible set is nonempty since every finite convex combination of points of $K$ is the barycenter of a finite atomic probability. The definition does not assert that the infimum is attained; the theorem on this page gives a compact continuous sufficient condition.

items.title: Elastic collision model and weak collision identity
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge2$. The **elastic collision set** is
$$Q_{m el}:=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{4d}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\},$$
with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. A collision measure is a nonnegative countably additive measure $
u$ on this measurable space. It is symmetric if it is invariant under the exchanges $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(w,v)$, $(v',w')\leftrightarrow(w',v')$, and $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(v',w')$. These invariances are hypotheses on $
u$, not consequences of energy and momentum conservation.

Fix the velocity measure space $(\mathbb R^d,\mathcal L(\mathbb R^d),dv)$, where $dv$ is the Lebesgue set function of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]] and its countably additive measure-space structure is assumed as part of the data. This definition makes no existence assertion for that structure or for the collision operator. An input density is a finite-valued positive Lebesgue-measurable function $f:\mathbb R^d	o(0,\infty)$ whose four coordinate evaluations $f(v),f(w),f(v'),f(w')$ on $Q_{m el}$ are $
u$-measurable. Let $\mathcal D_
u$ be a declared set of such inputs. Put $\mathcal L^1_{m loc}:=\{q:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R:q	ext{ is Lebesgue measurable and }\int_K|q|\,dv<\infty	ext{ for every compact }K\subset\mathbb R^d\}$. Its elements here are chosen function representatives, rather than equivalence classes. A collision model includes a specified map $Q_
u:\mathcal D_
u	o\mathcal L^1_{m loc}$; write $Q(f):=Q_
u(f)$.

For $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, put $A=f(v)f(w)$ and $B=f(v')f(w')$. For a finite-valued complex Lebesgue-measurable function $\varphi$ on velocity space, put $\delta\varphi:=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$. Define the complete admissible test class $\mathcal T_f$ to consist of exactly those $\varphi$ for which $\delta\varphi$ is $
u$-measurable and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\varphi(v)Q_
u(f)(v)|\,dv<\infty,\qquad \int_{Q_{m el}}|(B-A)\delta\varphi|\,d
u<\infty.$$
Absolute integrability is in the sense of [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. The model also declares, for each $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, a complex linear testing subspace $\mathcal S_f\subseteq\mathcal T_f$ containing at least one nonzero test. Require the following **weak collision identity** for every $f\in\mathcal D_
u$ and every $\varphi\in\mathcal S_f$. A formulation adopting all admissible tests specifies $\mathcal S_f=\mathcal T_f$; a result using only particular tests names those tests and their linear span explicitly:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(v)Q(f)(v)\,dv= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(f(v')f(w')-f(v)f(w))(\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w'))\,d
u,$$
Both sides are absolutely convergent by the test-class definition. Admissible tests need not be bounded or compactly supported: $1$, velocity coordinates, squared speed, and $\log(f/f_{m ref})$ for a positive constant $f_{m ref}$ belong to $\mathcal T_f$ whenever they meet the displayed measurability and integrability conditions. A consumer invoking one of these tests must establish or assume those conditions and require it to belong to the declared testing domain $\mathcal S_f$. In particular, the entropy branch uses the span of $1$ and $\log(f/f_{m ref})$, with absolute convergence explicitly assumed. The map $Q_
u$, its input domain and its testing domains are adopted model data; the weak identity is their admissibility condition, not an assertion that every positive density and collision measure admit such a map or that these tests alone uniquely determine it. Molecular chaos or a microscopic derivation of the identity is not part of the definition.

items.title: Finite-site canonical law and microcanonical shell
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix a finite alphabet $A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$, $q\ge1$, and real single-site energies $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ in a fixed energy unit. At inverse parameter $\beta\in\mathbb R$, define
$$Z_1(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^q e^{-\beta e_j},\qquad p_j(\beta):=e^{-\beta e_j}/Z_1(\beta),\qquad E(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^q p_j(\beta)e_j.$$
For $N\ge1$, a configuration $i=(i_1,\ldots,i_N)\in A^N$ has additive energy $H_N(i):=\sum_{r=1}^Ne_{i_r}$. Given a width $\delta_N\ge0$, the **shell** is
$$\Gamma_N(\beta,\delta_N):=\{i\in A^N:|H_N(i)-NE(\beta)|\le\delta_N\}.$$
When this finite set is nonempty, its microcanonical law means the uniform probability on $\Gamma_N$, and its dimensionless entropy is $\log|\Gamma_N|$. A type is a vector $t=(n_1/N,\ldots,n_q/N)$, where the nonnegative integer counts sum to $N$; its multiplicity is $N!/\prod_j n_j!$.

The convention fixes both the shell center and the law within the shell. It makes no physical claim that an apparatus has resolution $\delta_N$.

items.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck integral equation
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0},P)$ carry a standard Brownian motion $B$ adapted to the filtration, with future increments independent of the present sigma-algebra. Fix constants $\gamma>0$ and $\sigma>0$, and an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable real random variable $X_0$ with finite second moment. A **continuous adapted solution of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck equation** on $[0,T]$ is a continuous adapted process $X$ satisfying, almost surely for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$X_t=X_0-\gamma\int_0^tX_s\,ds+\sigma B_t,$$
where the time integral is the ordinary Lebesgue integral along the continuous path. In differential notation this is $dX_t=-\gamma X_t\,dt+\sigma\,dB_t$, with the stochastic differential interpreted through the displayed integral equation.

The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. The Itô integral in the explicit representation is the square-integrable predictable-process integral of [[def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes]].

items.title: Regular energy shell and weighted area measure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $O\subset\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge2$, be open, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. An energy $E\in J$ is **regular** if $\nabla H(x)\ne0$ for every $x\in\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$. By the implicit-function theorem, a neighborhood of each point of a nonempty regular level is a graph $x_i=h(z)$.

In a graph chart, use the local area density $\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(z)|^2}\,dz$, where $dz$ is $(m-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. A **graph partition** on $\Sigma_E$ is a locally finite graph-chart cover with nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_a$ supported in their respective charts and summing to one on the level. Whenever such a partition is supplied, define the candidate weighted shell integral by
$$\mu_E(g):=\sum_a\int g(z,h_a(z))\chi_a(z,h_a(z))|\partial_iH(z,h_a(z))|^{-1}\,dz$$
for nonnegative Borel $g$. Its independence from the chosen chart partition, and its equality with $\int_{\Sigma_E}g|\nabla H|^{-1}dA_E$, are proved in the theorem on this page. If $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, the **microcanonical shell probability** is $\widehat\mu_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$.

This is an explicit chart-based definition, not a formal delta distribution $\delta(H-E)$. Critical levels are excluded.

items.title: Continuous ideal-gas bulk limit and finite-block bridge
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix dimension $d\ge1$, particle mass $m>0$, action reference $h>0$, inverse energy $\beta>0$, and positive cube volumes $V_N$ with $N/V_N\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. For $N$ indistinguishable classical noninteracting particles in a cube of volume $V_N$, use the phase-space reference $dq\,dp/(N!h^{dN})$ and Hamiltonian $H_N(q,p)=\sum_{i=1}^N|p_i|^2/(2m)$. Define $\lambda_\beta=h\sqrt{\beta/(2\pi m)}$. Then the dimensionless partition integral and free-energy limits are
$$Z_N=\frac{V_N^N}{N!\lambda_\beta^{dN}},\quad\frac{-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N}{N}\longrightarrow\beta^{-1}[\log(\rho\lambda_\beta^d)-1],\quad\frac{-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N}{V_N}\longrightarrow\beta^{-1}\rho[\log(\rho\lambda_\beta^d)-1].$$
There is also the following finite-momentum-block limit. Let $M=dN$, let $G_1,\ldots,G_M$ be independent standard normal variables, set $A_N=M^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^MG_a^2$, and define canonical momenta $P_a^{\rm can}=\sqrt{m/\beta}\,G_a$ and shell-prepared momenta $P_a^{\rm sh}=\sqrt{m/\beta}\,G_a/\sqrt{A_N}$. On the null event $A_N=0$, set the shell-prepared vector to $(\sqrt{mM/\beta},0,\ldots,0)$. The shell-prepared vector has exactly energy $dN/(2\beta)$, and for every fixed $r$ and bounded continuous $\psi:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R$,
$$\mathbb E\psi(P_1^{\rm sh},\ldots,P_r^{\rm sh})\longrightarrow\mathbb E\psi(P_1^{\rm can},\ldots,P_r^{\rm can}).$$
This is weak convergence for each fixed block in this free-particle model. The shell preparation is the stated normalized-Gaussian construction, and no finite-width shell or interacting-gas equivalence is asserted.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-continuous-ideal-gas-block-limit.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Hamiltonian volume, recurrence, and ergodic scope
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a smooth $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, with Hamiltonian field defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. Wherever its local flow $\phi_t$ is defined, it preserves the symplectic form and the volume measure $m$ determined by $\omega^n/n!$. No completeness is asserted. Let $R$ be a measurable region on which a nonzero-time map $T=\phi_\tau$ is defined and is forward invariant, $T(R)\subseteq R$. The restriction $T:R\to R$ preserves $m|_R$ if $T(R)=R$, or more generally if $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$. This latter condition holds automatically when $m(R)<\infty$. Thus for every finite-measure forward-invariant $R$ and every measurable $E\subseteq R$, almost every point of $E$ returns to $E$ infinitely often under forward iteration. Mere forward invariance of an infinite-volume region does not imply relative measure preservation.

If $m(R)=1$ and $T$ is ergodic, then for every $f\in L^1(R,m)$ the averages $N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f(T^jx)$ converge almost everywhere and in $L^1$ to $\int_Rf\,dm$. Without ergodicity, the limit is the invariant conditional expectation supplied by Birkhoff's theorem, not necessarily the space mean. Finally, fix any real scalar $k_B$. If each stated time map $\phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism of a finite invariant region $R$, a density $p_0\ge0$ with $\int_Rp_0\,dm=1$ and $\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty$ transports by $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$ with conserved fine-grained entropy $-k_B\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm$, using $0\log0=0$. Volume preservation alone does not imply ergodicity or a time-average/ensemble identity.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence.md and its proof contract.

references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter read; §§8.1–8.3, Hamiltonian phase-space flow, Liouville theorem, and equilibration qualifications.

items.proof:
**Given:** [A1]–[A3] and the inspected supplier interfaces [F1]–[F6].

1.1 By [F1], $\omega$ is closed and $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. The Hamiltonian-flow theorem [F2], under its local existence domain, gives $\phi_t^*\omega=\omega$ and hence $\phi_t^*(\omega^n/n!)=\omega^n/n!$. The volume measure defined by this positive form is therefore preserved by each local flow diffeomorphism on its domain. For a measurable $E\subseteq R$, injectivity and volume preservation give $m((T|_R)^{-1}E)=m(E\cap T(R))$. If $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$, this equals $m(E)$, so the restriction is the measure-preserving system of [F3]. When $m(R)<\infty$, volume preservation gives $m(T(R))=m(R)$; because $T(R)\subseteq R$, finite additivity gives $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$. Thus the finite forward-invariant case follows without an onto hypothesis. Also $dH(X_H)=\omega(X_H,X_H)=0$ because a two-form is alternating, so each defined orbit stays on its energy level. This argument grants no flow outside its domain. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F3] to $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$. It preserves $\int p_t\,dm=\int p_0\,dm=1$. The scalar function $u\mapsto u\log u$, defined to be $0$ at $u=0$ by [A3], is Borel; its absolute integrability is preserved because the same measure-preserving substitution gives $$\int_R|p_t\log p_t|\,dm=\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty.$$ Applying integral invariance to its positive and negative parts proves $\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm=\int_Rp_0\log p_0\,dm$. Multiplication by the fixed real scalar $-k_B$ gives the stated scaled entropy conservation. [A2, A3, F3, F6, step 1.1]

2.2 The map $T$ on $R$ is measure preserving by 1.1 and [A2]. Its total measure is finite, so [F4] gives infinite returns for almost every point in each measurable $E\subseteq R$. The conclusion is explicitly almost everywhere and applies to the sampled map at the specified $\tau$. [A2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Under the additional probability and ergodicity assumptions in [A2], the hypotheses of [F5] hold for each $f\in L^1(R,m)$. Birkhoff therefore gives almost-everywhere and $L^1$ convergence to the invariant conditional expectation, and its ergodic corollary identifies that limit with $\int_R f\,dm$. If ergodicity is removed, only the invariant conditional expectation conclusion remains. Neither [F2] nor recurrence [F4] supplies ergodicity. [A2, F5, step 1.1] ∎

items.title: Attainment and finite support for compact continuous mixtures
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact, $d\ge1$, and $a:K\to\mathbb R$ continuous. Define $a_{\rm mix}$ as in [[def-tdmath-mixture-generator-space-and-energy]]. Then for every $x\in\operatorname{conv}K$ the infimum defining $a_{\rm mix}(x)$ is attained by a Borel probability measure supported on at most $d+1$ points. The function $a_{\rm mix}$ is lower semicontinuous and convex on $\operatorname{conv}K$, and is the greatest convex function on $\operatorname{conv}K$ bounded above by $a$ on $K$. Minimizing over all Borel probabilities on $K$ gives the same attained value as minimizing over finite mixtures. This is a mathematical compactness result; it makes no phase-preparation or equilibrium postulate.

items.title: Finite-site microcanonical and canonical block equivalence
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$, $q\ge1$, have real energies $e_j$, and fix finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Set $Z_1=\sum_j e^{-\beta e_j}$, $p_j=e^{-\beta e_j}/Z_1>0$, and $E=\sum_jp_je_j$. For each $N\ge1$, let $\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|$ and $\delta_N/N\to0$. Define the shell $\Gamma_N=\{i\in A^N:|\sum_{r=1}^Ne_{i_r}-NE|\le\delta_N\}$ and the uniform law on that shell. For probability laws $\mu,\nu$ on the finite set $A^k$, total variation distance means $\frac12\sum_{x\in A^k}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$. Then $\Gamma_N$ is nonempty for every $N$; for each fixed $k\ge1$, the first $k$-site marginal (for $N\ge k$) converges in that distance to $p^{\otimes k}$; and
$$\frac1N\log|\Gamma_N|\longrightarrow H(p):=-\sum_{j=1}^qp_j\log p_j.$$
The conclusion is for this finite alphabet, additive energy, exact shell width and uniform shell law. It does not assert finite-size equality or equivalence for interacting or continuous models.

items.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck equation, transition law, and fluctuations
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Assume the filtered probability space, Brownian increment hypothesis, and initial data of [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]], including $\mathbb E X_0^2<\infty$ and future increments independent of $\mathcal F_0$. For $\gamma,\sigma>0$, on every finite time interval the process
$$X_t=e^{-\gamma t}X_0+\sigma e^{-\gamma t}\int_0^t e^{\gamma s}\,dB_s$$
has a continuous adapted version, solves the stated Ornstein–Uhlenbeck integral equation, and is the unique continuous solution driven by the same $(X_0,B)$. Put $V=\sigma^2/(2\gamma)$. For $0\le s<t$, its transition law conditional on $\mathcal F_s$ is normal with mean $e^{-\gamma(t-s)}X_s$ and variance $V(1-e^{-2\gamma(t-s)})$. Consequently
$$\mathbb E X_t=e^{-\gamma t}\mathbb E X_0,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=e^{-2\gamma t}\operatorname{Var}(X_0)+V(1-e^{-2\gamma t}).$$
From any such initial law, $X_t$ converges in distribution to $N(0,V)$. If $X_0\sim N(0,V)$ and is independent of future Brownian increments, the process is stationary Gaussian with covariance $C(\tau)=Ve^{-\gamma|\tau|}$, and its transition kernel satisfies detailed balance with the $N(0,V)$ density. Its transition density solves the Fokker–Planck equation for positive time. Under the convention $S(\omega)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}C(\tau)e^{i\omega\tau}\,d\tau$, the stationary spectrum and time-average bound are
$$S(\omega)=\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)},\qquad\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1T\int_0^T X_t\,dt\right)\le\frac{2V}{\gamma T}.$$
All these statements concern the specified linear stochastic model. An Einstein relation between $\sigma$ and a physical bath temperature would be an additional physical postulate.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-model.md and its proof contract.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 3
references.locator: Complete 26-page lecture-note part retrieved and read; §§3.1.2–3.2.3, pp.54–70, Langevin dynamics, velocity diffusion, and Fokker–Planck equation.

items.proof:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, [A1]–[A2], and [F1]–[F7].

1.1 On $[0,T]$, $g(s)=e^{\gamma s}$ is deterministic, continuous, and square-integrable. Thus $W_t=\int_0^t g(s)\,dB_s$ is defined by [F3], and [F4] supplies a continuous version. For a partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_n=t$, the deterministic step sums $\sum_k g(t_k)(B_{t_{k+1}}-B_{t_k})$ converge in $L^2$ to $W_t$ by the Itô isometry and uniform approximation of $g$. Discrete summation by parts rewrites them as $g(t)B_t-g(0)B_0-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}B_{t_{k+1}}(g(t_{k+1})-g(t_k))$ up to an endpoint term tending to zero. Brownian path continuity makes the last sums converge pathwise to $\int_0^t g'(s)B_sds$. The $L^2$ limit and this almost-sure limit agree in probability, so $$W_t=e^{\gamma t}B_t-\gamma\int_0^t e^{\gamma s}B_s\,ds$$ almost surely for each fixed $t$. Both sides have continuous versions; equality on rational $t$ holds on one probability-one event and therefore extends to all $t\in[0,T]$. [A1, A2, F2, F3, F4, F5]

1.2 Split the stochastic integral at $s$ and use its linearity: $$X_t=e^{-\gamma(t-s)}X_s+\sigma\int_s^t e^{-\gamma(t-u)}\,dB_u.$$ Step-function approximants to the last deterministic-integrand integral depend only on increments after $s$, so [A1] makes them independent of $\mathcal F_s$. Their $L^2$ limit remains independent of $\mathcal F_s$: for bounded $\mathcal F_s$-measurable $Y$ and bounded continuous $\varphi$, convergence in probability plus boundedness gives convergence of $\mathbb E[Y\varphi(\cdot)]$, preserving the factorization. By [F4] the limit is centered Gaussian; [F3] computes its variance as $\sigma^2\int_s^t e^{-2\gamma(t-u)}du=V(1-e^{-2\gamma(t-s)})$. This proves the conditional transition law and the Markov property. [A1, A2, F3, F4]

2.1 Set $X_t=e^{-\gamma t}X_0+\sigma e^{-\gamma t}W_t$. By [F4] it is continuous and adapted. Step 1.1 rewrites it as $$X_t=e^{-\gamma t}X_0+\sigma B_t-\sigma\gamma\int_0^t e^{-\gamma(t-s)}B_s\,ds.$$ Integrating this continuous expression in $t$, ordinary Fubini [F5] gives $$\int_0^tX_sds=X_0(1-e^{-\gamma t})/\gamma+\sigma\int_0^tB_sds-\sigma\int_0^tB_u(1-e^{-\gamma(t-u)})\,du.$$ Substitution into $X_0-\gamma\int_0^tX_sds+\sigma B_t$ cancels the two $\int B_sds$ terms and leaves exactly the displayed expression for $X_t$. Thus [F1] holds. [A1, A2, F1, F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 Taking expectations in the explicit solution, the stochastic integral has mean zero by [F4], giving $\mathbb E X_t=e^{-\gamma t}\mathbb E X_0$. The integral is independent of $X_0$ and centered, so its variance adds to $e^{-2\gamma t}\operatorname{Var}(X_0)$; [F3] evaluates the added variance as $V(1-e^{-2\gamma t})$. The independent Gaussian term tends in law to $N(0,V)$ because its variance tends to $V$ and $e^{-\gamma t}X_0\to0$ in $L^2$; for any bounded continuous test, restrict to a compact interval, use uniform continuity and the second-moment tail bound, then take the interval radius to infinity. [A1, A2, F3, F4, step 1.2]

2.3 Write $r=e^{-\gamma t}$ and $\pi(x)=(2\pi V)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/(2V)}$. The transition density is $$K_t(x,y)=[2\pi V(1-r^2)]^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-rx)^2}{2V(1-r^2)}\right).$$ Multiplying by $\pi(x)$ gives a symmetric prefactor and exponent proportional to $-[x^2+y^2-2rxy]/[2V(1-r^2)]$, unchanged when $x$ and $y$ are exchanged. Hence $\pi(x)K_t(x,y)=\pi(y)K_t(y,x)$, the detailed-balance identity. [A1, A2, F6, F7, step 1.2]

2.4 For $t>0$ let $\mu=e^{-\gamma t}x$, $v=V(1-e^{-2\gamma t})$, and $p(t,x,y)$ be the normal density with mean $\mu$ and variance $v$. Direct differentiation gives $$\partial_t p=p\left(\frac{\mu'(y-\mu)}v+\frac{v'}2\left[\frac{(y-\mu)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right]\right),\quad \mu'=-\gamma\mu,\quad v'=\sigma^2-2\gamma v.$$ Also direct $y$-differentiation gives $\gamma\partial_y(yp)+(\sigma^2/2)\partial_{yy}p$ equal to the same expression after writing $y=\mu+(y-\mu)$. Thus $\partial_t p=\gamma\partial_y(yp)+(\sigma^2/2)\partial_{yy}p$. The Gaussian formula has total integral one and converges to point mass at $x$ as $t\downarrow0$; this is the stated positive-time Fokker–Planck solution. [A2, F5, F7, step 1.2]

3.1 If $X$ and $\widetilde X$ are two continuous solutions with the same data, their difference $z$ satisfies $z(t)=-\gamma\int_0^tz(s)ds$. Let $D(t)=\int_0^t|z(s)|ds$. Then $D(0)=0$, $D\ge0$, and $D'(t)=|z(t)|\le\gamma D(t)$ by the equation. The derivative of $e^{-\gamma t}D(t)$ is nonpositive, so this nonnegative function is at most its initial value zero. Hence $D=0$ and continuity gives $z=0$ at every time. [A2, F1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 If $X_0$ is centered normal with variance $V$, step 1.2 gives centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws, since each stochastic integral over a disjoint increment interval is an independent Gaussian and $X_0$ is independent of future increments. Its one-time variance is $V$. For $s\le t$, the split formula in 2.1 and independence of the later increment yield $\mathbb E[X_sX_t]=e^{-\gamma(t-s)}\mathbb E[X_s^2]=Ve^{-\gamma(t-s)}$. Thus covariance depends only on $|t-s|$. A centered Gaussian finite-dimensional law is determined by its covariance matrix; shifting every time by the same amount preserves that matrix and proves stationarity. [A1, A2, F4, step 1.2, step 2.2]

4.1 For $R>0$, the derivative and componentwise FTC in [F6] give $\int_0^R e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt=(1-e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R})/(\gamma-i\omega)$. The modulus formula gives $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R}|=e^{-\gamma R}\to0$ and $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}|=e^{-\gamma t}$, whose integral is finite. Thus the stationary covariance is integrable. By evenness, $$S(\omega)=\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt =\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac1{\gamma-i\omega} =\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)}.$$ The integral converges absolutely because $\gamma>0$. [A2, F6, step 3.2]

5.1 For the stationary time average, Fubini applies to the random product because $\mathbb E|X_sX_t|\le(\mathbb E X_s^2\mathbb E X_t^2)^{1/2}=V$, so its absolute integral over the finite square and probability space is at most $VT^2$. Changing variables in the two triangular halves gives $$\operatorname{Var}\!\left(T^{-1}\int_0^TX_tdt\right) =\frac{2V}{T^2}\int_0^T(T-s)e^{-\gamma s}ds \le\frac{2V}{\gamma T}.$$ The bound tends to zero, so these averages converge to zero in $L^2$ and in probability. It asserts no almost-sure theorem for arbitrary observables. [A1, A2, F5, step 3.2] ∎

items.title: Conditional Boltzmann entropy inequality and equality form
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix periods $L_1,\ldots,L_d>0$, let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ with quotient Lebesgue measure $dr$, let $d\ge2$, and let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open time interval. Suppose $f:\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d	imes I	o(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ in space and time and $C^2$ in velocity. Fix a positive constant reference density $f_{m ref}$ with the same units as $f$, and put $\ell(r,v,t)=\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{m ref})$. For each $t\in I$, assume $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d$. For every compact interval $I_0\subset I$, assume there is a nonnegative $G_{I_0}\in L^1(\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d,dr\,dv)$ such that $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|\le G_{I_0}$ almost everywhere for every $t\in I_0$. Also assume $(1+|\ell|)|v\cdot
abla_r f|\in L^1(\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d,dr\,dv)$ for each $t\in I$. Write $A=f(r,v,t)f(r,w,t)$ and $B=f(r,v',t)f(r,w',t)$. For each $t\in I$, assume $r\mapsto\int_{Q_{m el}}|(A-B)(\ell(r,v,t)+\ell(r,w,t)-\ell(r,v',t)-\ell(r,w',t))|\,d
u$ is measurable and belongs to $L^1(\Omega,dr)$. Let $Q$ and the symmetric collision measure $
u$ satisfy the weak identity in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]] for tests $1$ and $\ell(r,\cdot,t)$ at each $(r,t)$, with absolute convergence, and suppose
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot
abla_r f=Q(f).$$
Then for $H[f](t)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\ell\,dv\,dr$,
$$ rac{d}{dt}H[f](t)=- rac14\int_\Omega\int_{Q_{m el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d
u\,dr\le0.$$
The integrand is nonnegative because $\log$ is strictly increasing. Equality in the entropy-production integral holds exactly when $A=B$ for $
u$-almost every collision at almost every $r$. Under the additional assumptions that $
u$ is locally finite, has full support on $Q_{m el}$, and $f$ is positive and $C^2$ in $v$, this balance implies for almost every $r$ that
$$\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{m ref})=\alpha(r,t)+b(r,t)\cdot v+ rac{\lambda(r,t)}2|v|^2.$$
If $f(r,\cdot,t)$ is integrable over $\mathbb R^d$, then $\lambda(r,t)<0$, so its velocity profile is Maxwellian. Conversely, every profile of this form has zero collision entropy production. The weak collision identity is an explicit model hypothesis; this is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a PDE existence theorem.

items.title: Coarea and invariant measure on compact regular energy shells
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Trace-norm Cesàro dephasing for a discrete Gibbs spectrum
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the exact first-clause interface of [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]]: a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a finite or countable complete orthonormal energy eigenbasis $(u_j)$ for a self-adjoint semibounded $A$, with each energy eigenspace finite-dimensional. The supplier is a current draft whose statement and complete argument have been inspected; this theorem is conditional on that interface and does not claim its independent acceptance. Let $\hbar>0$, define $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and extend linearly and continuously. For any positive trace-class density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, set $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$. If $P_E$ denotes the projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$, then the trace-norm Riemann average
$$\bar\rho_T:=\frac1T\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$$
converges as $T\to\infty$ to
$$\rho_{\rm diag}:=\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$
in trace norm. The full degenerate energy blocks are retained. Thus expectations of every bounded observable converge to their diagonal-ensemble values. This asserts Cesàro convergence, not convergence of $\rho_t$ at individual late times, and is restricted to the stated discrete trace-class spectrum.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Pure-state entropy and entropy of a dephased average
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Use $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with $\langle z,w\rangle=z_1\overline{w_1}+z_2\overline{w_2}$, linear in the first argument, and $u_1=(1,0)$, $u_2=(0,1)$. Choose real $E_1\ne E_2$ and define the self-adjoint energy operator $A(z_1,z_2)=(E_1z_1,E_2z_2)$. Fix $\hbar>0$, set $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and define $P_jz=\langle z,u_j\rangle u_j$, $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$ and $\bar\rho_T=T^{-1}\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$. Let $\psi=(u_1+u_2)/\sqrt2$, $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$. Define the finite-dimensional entropy of a density matrix with eigenvalues $p_i$ as $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_i p_i\log p_i$, with $0\log0=0$ and fixed $k_B>0$. Every instantaneous unitary state $\rho_t$ is pure and has entropy zero. The Cesàro states converge to $\rho_{\rm diag}=(P_1+P_2)/2$, whose entropy is $k_B\log2$. In fact $S(\bar\rho_T)\to k_B\log2$, whereas $T^{-1}\int_0^T S(\rho_t)\,dt=0$ for every $T$. Entropy of the averaged state and average instantaneous entropy are distinct quantities.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/ex-tdmath-pure-state-versus-average-entropy.md and its proof contract.
